sections.heading: Network Status Updates
sections.summary: Heze devnets 2 and 3 are stable aside from getPayload timeout issues; Sepolia and Glamsterdam devnets remain stable; Bogota devnet 1 onboarding Nimbus EL.
sections.body:
- Heze devnet 2 and devnet 3 have been spammed to stress-test the network; only notable issue is the getPayload timeout problem (discussed later in the call).
- Sepolia and Glamsterdam devnets are both stable.
- Hoodi fork was originally scheduled for today (~4-5 hours after the call) but will not happen due to the postponement.
- Bogota devnet 1 is still running; Nimbus EL is being onboarded after some issues were fixed.
  - Fuzzing has not yet been run on Bogota devnet 1, but tests should be ready today or tomorrow.
  - Bogota devnet 2 launch still requires some client branches.

sections.heading: EIP-8037/EIP-8038 Interaction Issues
sections.summary: ChainSecurity reported four vulnerability patterns from EIP-8037/8038 opcode interactions; audits are underway and Hoodi scheduling is delayed at least two weeks.
sections.body:
- ChainSecurity reported that EIP-8037 and EIP-8038 interact with opcodes in unanticipated ways, surfacing four distinct issue categories:
  - Known issue: hard-coded gas values in contracts breaking after opcode repricing.
  - New finding: `gasLeft` can suddenly increase, which was not anticipated.
  - New finding: refunds can fund execution paths that were previously unreachable.
  - Multiple coding patterns identified as breaking independently.
- Over the weekend, extensive analysis was performed (including AI-assisted scans of every contract verified on Sourcify) and the blast radius appears well understood.
  - Francesco D'Amato noted in chat that the vast majority of findings are about repricings and that nothing meaningful has been found in two days of continued analysis.
- ChainSecurity and Dedaub have been engaged for a comprehensive audit; ETA is approximately two weeks from today.
- Agreement: Hoodi scheduling should be delayed until at least the audits complete; no spec changes should be the default approach.
  - Maria Silva outlined the strategy: identify affected contracts, reach out to teams, ask if they can fix on their side; only consider spec changes as a last resort for unfixable, high-blast-radius cases.
  - Spec changes are expensive — in many cases would require undoing entire EIPs, redoing Sepolia, creating new tests, and another security review.
  - Any spec changes should be targeted and modular, not bundled, to avoid cascading breakage.
- Łukasz Rozmej has an open PR exploring potential spec changes as a parallel track, built from 12+ hours of cross-model AI analysis.
  - Maria Silva is reviewing and breaking it down into per-invariant targeted fixes for use only if needed.
- Fredrik posted [a PR to reduce risk of similar issues recurring](https://github.com/ethereum/pm/pull/2284) and asked for feedback.
- Potuz suggested that if a major spec change is needed, it may be better to ditch the EIP entirely.
- Barnabas asked in chat what the cost of pulling EIP-8037 from the fork would be; Maria Silva and others noted the biggest cost would be not being able to raise the gas limit safely, making optimizations like BAL meaningless.

sections.heading: Builder Onboarding Logic Change
sections.summary: Broad CL client support for changing builder onboarding so only 0x0B-prefixed deposits are credited to builders at fork transition; PR to be merged this week.
sections.body:
- Dima Gusakov (Lido) presented [consensus-specs PR #5736](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5736) to fix a broken invariant in the builder onboarding process at the Glamsterdam fork.
  - Current spec: deposits queued pre-Glamsterdam for a validator whose public key was front-run with a 0x0B-prefixed withdrawal credential deposit would be credited to a builder instead of creating a validator.
  - This breaks a fundamental assumption used by staking protocols (including Lido) that a deposit will always result in a validator appearing in the registry.
- Proposed fix: only deposits explicitly containing the 0x0B prefix in withdrawal credentials are credited to builders at fork time; all other deposits proceed normally through the validator deposit queue.
  - Potuz researched the change and found no issues beyond builders needing awareness of top-up behavior.
- Support expressed from: Prysm (Potuz), Lighthouse (Pawan), Lodestar (Nico, cayman), Nimbus (Dustin conditionally).
  - Dustin's concern was about Sepolia compatibility for genesis sync / backfilling; confirmed that no builder onboardings occurred on Sepolia, so this change has no impact there.
- No objections raised.
- Decision: merge the PR and cut a spec release this week.

sections.heading: getPayload Timeout Removal
sections.summary: A merged execution-APIs PR removes the getPayload timeout; ELs should respond immediately with the best available payload rather than waiting.
sections.body:
- Barnabas introduced [execution-APIs PR #958](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/pull/958), which removes the getPayload timeout definition, requiring ELs to reply as soon as possible.
  - The PR was already merged by Mikhail before full discussion.
- Multiple EL clients (Besu, Reth, Ethrex) had issues on devnets where getPayload responses were delayed or timing out because they were intentionally waiting to build more valuable blocks.
  - Daniel Lehrner (Besu) confirmed the behavior was intentional but acknowledged the spec now clarifies that instant response is expected.
  - Geth always returns the current payload immediately, falling back to empty if the full one isn't built yet.
- Dustin noted this clarifies intent: Nimbus CL saw consistent getPayload timeouts from Reth on devnets and couldn't tell if the delay was a bug or spec-allowed behavior.
- Fabio (Besu) raised a FOCIL interaction concern: with inclusion lists, returning an empty block is worthless since it won't satisfy the IL; the first response may need to include at least the IL transactions, causing slight delay.
- Nico (Lodestar) asked about CL calling strategy: if builders are configured, CL could delay getPayload until after getHeader returns to give EL maximum build time.
- Potuz expressed concern this change may break FCU timings on Prysm and noted that FOCIL and shorter slots need to be thought through carefully with respect to this interaction.
- No formal objections raised, but Justin Traglia asked everyone to review the merged PR and noted it can be unmerged if needed; further discussion expected at Devcon or next ACDT.

sections.heading: Skipping ACDT on November 2nd for Devcon

sections.body:

sections.heading: Verifying Backfilled Envelopes for Exited Builders
sections.summary: Envelope signatures cannot be verified for exited builders during backfill; Nimbus will open a spec PR clarifying that signature verification is not required for backfilled envelopes.
sections.body:
- Sam (Nimbus) raised an issue about verifying payload envelope signatures during backfill sync when the builder has already exited and the state is no longer available.
  - Pawan (Lighthouse) confirmed the same issue: verifying the signature requires builder state that may not exist post-exit.
- Potuz argued that envelope signatures should never need verification during backfill — the signature exists solely for gossip-time DoS protection; receivers during backfill should rely on the block hash alone.
- Dustin agreed the spec should make this explicit:
  - Block backfill spec (since Phase 0) clearly states signatures must be verified, but there is no analogous language for envelopes.
  - Proposed that if signatures aren't meaningful for backfill, the spec should either say so explicitly or define the signature field as zero for backfilled envelopes.
- Sam will open a consensus-specs PR to add a clarification that envelope signatures are not required for verification during backfill.
  - Potuz, Pawan, and Justin Traglia expressed support.
  - Pawan and Justin Traglia volunteered to review the PR.

sections.heading: Gas Limit Gossip Check for Payload Transactions
sections.summary: Nico proposed a CL gossip check limiting payload transaction count based on gas limit; concerns about cross-layer constants remain but a PR will be opened.
sections.body:
- Nico (Lodestar) proposed adding a CL-side gossip validation check: `len(payload.transactions) <= bid.gas_limit // MIN_TRANSACTION_GAS`.
  - This would allow early rejection of oversized or malicious payloads during deserialization/gossip, before forwarding to the EL.
  - With ePBS, it's easier to broadcast invalid payloads; this check hardens the P2P gossip layer.
- If specified in the spec, invalid payloads can trigger peer downscoring (reject); without spec backing, clients can only silently ignore.
- Toni Wahrstätter raised concerns about coupling CL with EL-specific constants:
  - Minimum transaction gas changes across forks (21,000 pre-Glamsterdam, 12,000 post-Glamsterdam per [EIP-2780](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-2780)).
  - Will likely change again with frame transactions.
- Potuz suggested using a very conservative lower bound (e.g., 1,000 gas) that wouldn't need frequent updates but would still prevent the worst DoS scenarios.
- No PR exists yet; Nico to open one.
  - Justin Traglia suggested opening it for further discussion and potential merge soon.

sections.heading: Shorter Slots Spec Merging Strategy
sections.summary: No consensus on merging shorter slots into the main Heze spec; it will remain a feature branch until more client teams agree and potentially until SFI at ACD.
sections.body:
- Barnabas asked whether shorter slots should be merged into the main Heze consensus spec, noting 4 client implementations already exist and Heze devnet 3 already runs with quick slots (9-second slot duration).
  - 3 separate PRs exist for the quick slots implementation, creating confusion about which commit hash to target for testing.
- Potuz opposed merging into main spec before SFI, arguing that features not scheduled for inclusion should not be on the main branch, and that feature authors should maintain their own rebased branch/tag for test vectors.
  - Merging would force all subsequent features to build on top, effectively cementing the proposal before an SFI decision.
- Matthew Keil (Lodestar) said the main contention is merging with a changed slot time (e.g., 10 seconds), not the machinery itself; merging with unchanged times (6s minimal, 12s mainnet) would be more acceptable.
- Potuz noted that changing the minimal spec times would break Prysm's testing — they'd be forced to have shorter slots on their trunk branch or skip tests.
- Barnabas proposed merging the machinery with unchanged times (6/12 seconds), which would "break nothing."
- Justin Traglia's position: until a majority of clients agree to merge it into Heze, it should remain a feature; SFI is not required for merge, but broad client support is.
- Mehdi Aouadi (Teku) noted FOCIL followed the same pattern — tested but not merged until SFI'd.
- Decision deferred to further Discord discussion and ACDC.
